title: Best AI presentation makers in 2026: Gamma, Canva, Copilot and more
excerpt: Gamma, Beautiful.ai, Pitch, Canva, Copilot in PowerPoint and Gemini in Slides compared on price, AI credits, exports and brand control for 2026.
content:
The best AI presentation maker in 2026 depends on where your slides have to end up. Gamma is the fastest way to turn a prompt or document into a polished deck, Beautiful.ai and Pitch suit teams that care about brand control and sharing, Canva is the easy choice if you already design there, and Copilot in PowerPoint or Gemini in Google Slides make sense when the final file must stay in Microsoft or Google formats. All prices below come from vendor pages checked on 4 October 2026.

Key takeaways

  • Gamma's paid plans start at $9 per seat a month on annual billing, and its free plan includes 400 one-time AI credits and export to PowerPoint, PDF and Google Slides.
  • Beautiful.ai Pro is $14.50 a month billed annually, Pitch Plus is $13 a month paid yearly, and Canva Pro is US$144 a year for one person.
  • Copilot in PowerPoint and Gemini in Google Slides now build whole decks from a prompt, but both need a qualifying paid Microsoft or Google plan.
  • Most tools meter AI through monthly credits, so compare the allowance, not just the headline price.
  • Vendor risk is real: Tome's founders walked away from a presentation app with 20 million users to build a CRM, according to Lightfield.

How we compared AI presentation tools

We take no affiliate fees and did not receive free accounts from any vendor here. Instead of scoring decks on taste, we compared what each company publishes on its own pricing and help pages, against five practical criteria for founders and marketers:

  • Output you can edit. Can you fix a slide by hand after the AI drafts it, and export to PowerPoint (PPTX), PDF or Google Slides?
  • Brand control. Custom themes, fonts, logos and templates, so a sales deck does not look like a template gallery.
  • AI allowance. Credits or usage limits included in each plan.
  • Sharing and analytics. Useful for fundraising and sales decks, where you want to know who opened what.
  • Transparent price. Whether you can buy without a sales call.

If you want to run your own test, give every tool the same brief and the same source document, such as last quarter's investor update, and time how long it takes to reach a deck you would actually send. Then export it to PPTX or PDF and open it on another machine. The editing time after the first draft, not the draft itself, is usually what separates the tools.

Gamma: fastest from idea to first draft

Gamma turns a prompt, outline or uploaded file into a deck, document or simple website, and it is the tool most founders try first. Its pricing page lists a free plan with 400 credits at sign-up (they do not refill), up to 10 slides per prompt, import from PDF and PPTX, and export to PDF, PPTX, PNG and Google Slides. Plus costs $9 per seat a month ($108 a year), with 1,000 monthly credits, up to 100 slides per prompt and no Gamma branding. Pro is $18 ($216 a year) and adds 4,000 credits, custom branding, detailed analytics, custom domains and API access. Ultra, at $90, is for heavy users who want 20,000 credits and the most advanced models.

Gamma says it uses models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, plus image models such as Flux, Ideogram and Leonardo. Unused credits roll over up to twice the monthly amount, and customers in India can pay by UPI, India's instant bank-transfer system. The company is also on solid footing: TechCrunch reported in November 2025 that Gamma raised a $68 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $2.1 billion valuation, and CEO Grant Lee said it had passed $100 million in annual recurring revenue profitably, with 70 million users.

Watch out for: Gamma's card-based layouts look best when presented inside Gamma or as a link. If investors or clients expect a conventional PPTX, export early and check the formatting.

Beautiful.ai and Pitch: brand control and team decks

Beautiful.ai

Beautiful.ai's selling point is "Smart Slides" that rearrange themselves as you add content, which stops decks drifting off-brand. According to its pricing page, Pro costs $14.50 a month for individuals, billed annually, and teams of two to 20 pay $40 per user a month billed annually or $50 monthly. Every seat includes unlimited AI content generation, more than 300 Smart Slide layouts, AI image generation, an AI writing assistant, translation and a custom theme builder. There is a 14-day free trial.

It suits teams that send many similar decks, such as sales proposals or monthly reports, where consistency matters more than creative freedom.

Pitch

Pitch is built for teams editing decks together. Its pricing page lists a free plan with unlimited presentations and 100 AI credits that do not renew. Paid plans, quoted per month when paying yearly, are Plus at $13 (500 AI credits a month, custom fonts, video uploads and PowerPoint export without Pitch branding), Team at $19 (tracked links, three teamspaces and shared "pitch rooms") and Business at $25 (750 credits and unlimited tracked links). A "Pitch Agent" generates presentations, and the company says more than 4 million teams use the product.

The tracked links are the practical draw for founders: you can see visits, slide views and time spent, which helps when following up with investors or prospects.

Canva: if your brand already lives there

Canva's presentations page describes Canva AI's Guided Presentations, which asks about audience, style and length, builds an outline you can reorder, then generates an editable deck. Exports include PowerPoint, PDF, video and a Canva website. Free accounts get a limited number of AI uses.

On its pricing page, Canva Pro costs US$144 a year for one person with ten times the AI usage of the free plan, while Canva Business is US$250 a year per person with 20 times the free allowance and up to 100 brand kits. Canva also notes that the law on who owns copyright in AI-generated content is unclear; it says it makes no copyright claim over what you generate, subject to its terms.

Copilot in PowerPoint and Gemini in Google Slides

For many companies the deck has to end up as a PowerPoint or Google Slides file anyway. Both suites now generate full decks from a prompt.

Copilot in PowerPoint

Microsoft's support page explains that you open Copilot in PowerPoint, choose Agent Mode and describe the deck. Copilot may ask about audience and style, produces an outline you can refine, then builds the slides. It works best from a Word document that uses proper heading styles and is under 24 MB, and starting from your organisation's template keeps its theme. AI images carry C2PA content credentials, an industry standard for labelling generated media. Microsoft notes limits too: one output language per prompt, and you cannot add extra context in the same prompt when you reference a file.

Pricing sits on the Copilot pricing page: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business is $21 per user a month paid yearly, with a first-year promotional price of $18 for eligible customers between 1 July and 31 December 2026. Solo users can get Copilot in PowerPoint through Microsoft 365 Personal at $99.99 a year.

Gemini in Google Slides

Google's help page says Gemini can generate fully editable presentations. You describe the deck, optionally add Drive files as sources, and can upload an existing deck so Gemini matches its style. Gemini then shows a plan with an overview, sources and a slide-by-slide outline that you approve before it builds. The feature is currently desktop-only and English-only, and needs an eligible Workspace or Google AI plan. Workspace Business Standard, the first tier with Gemini across Docs and other apps, is $14 per user a month at standard pricing.

General assistants are moving into slides as well. Anthropic's pricing page, for example, lists Claude Slides among the features of its $20-a-month Pro plan.

A warning about vendor risk

AI presentation tools are a crowded market, and not every product survives. Tome was one of the best-known early AI deck makers; Lightfield, the company its founders went on to build, describes the move on its press page as ditching a viral presentation app with 20 million users to build an AI-native CRM. The lesson for a startup is simple: keep master copies of important decks, such as your fundraising deck and board updates, in an exportable format, and test the PPTX or PDF export before you commit a team to any tool.

Which AI presentation maker should you choose?

  • Fundraising deck on a deadline: draft in Gamma or Pitch, then export and polish. Pitch's tracked links help with investor follow-ups. See who is raising on our funding tracker.
  • Sales team sending many proposals: Beautiful.ai or Pitch Business for templates and consistency.
  • Marketing team already designing in Canva: Canva Pro or Business, so decks share your brand kit.
  • Company standardised on Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace: Copilot or Gemini, so files stay in the formats clients and IT expect.

Whichever you choose, the AI draft is a starting point. Check every number, chart and claim, because the tools can produce confident-looking slides with wrong figures. For more on new AI products, see our launches and news pages.

Bottom line

For most founders, Gamma is the best first try for speed, Pitch for team decks with analytics, Beautiful.ai for strict brand consistency and Canva for design-led marketing material. If your company already pays for Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, test Copilot or Gemini before adding another subscription. Budget by credits, keep exportable copies, and review every slide by hand.

FAQ

What is the best free AI presentation maker?

Gamma, Pitch and Canva all have free plans. Gamma gives 400 one-time credits, Pitch gives 100 AI credits that do not renew, and Canva offers a limited number of AI uses.

Can AI presentation tools export to PowerPoint?

Yes. Gamma, Pitch (on paid plans without branding) and Canva export to PPTX, and Copilot works inside PowerPoint itself. Always check formatting after export.

Is Gamma better than PowerPoint Copilot?

Gamma is faster for a first draft and cheaper for individuals. Copilot is better when the final file must be a native PowerPoint deck using your company template.

Does Google Slides have AI deck generation?

Yes. Gemini in Google Slides can generate full, editable presentations from a prompt and Drive files, on desktop and in English, with an eligible Workspace or Google AI plan.

Who owns the copyright in AI-generated slides?

The law is unsettled. Canva, for example, says it makes no copyright claim over AI output you create, subject to its terms. Check each tool's terms for commercial use.
